catalog_quote: The most problematic feature of the vowels in my data on Sori concerns stress, which was intially recorded as penultimate. This pattern seems to represent the default case in the language, but some forms were recorded with antepenultimate or final stress, as with [bárawiɁ] ‘trivet, three stones of the hearth’, [báhawaj] ‘sugarcane’, [mwíhinoŋ] ‘stern of a canoe’, or [mbruwéj] ‘crocodile’, [uhúɁ] ‘cough’, [hotów] ‘hiccup’. However, apparent stress contrasts as in saŋóp ‘ten’ vs. húŋop ‘twenty’ suggest that stress is variable, and I therefore tentatively conclude that Sori does not have phonemic stress. Another indication that this probably is the correct analysis is that the three speakers of Lindrou with whom I worked were insistent on the placement of stress in their language, whereas the single speaker of Sori was not. audit.reasoning: (1) Quote confirmed verbatim at the stated place (p. 238, sec. 4.2) in the held PDF/text. (2) The deciding source is the only description of the language that exists: a 2021 sketch by Blust from 1975 fieldnotes (two days, one teenage speaker). Glottolog 5.1 has zero grammar/phonology/sketch entries for sori1242 besides it; Ross 1988 (fetched sources and grepped) is silent on Sori stress; So the best available source is held and quoted. (3) The coding VARIABLE follows Blust's own words ('stress is variable... tentatively conclude that Sori does not have phonemic stress'), with the hedged penultimate default recorded in prule; readers A and B already logged the defensible alternatives (hedged fixed-penultimate or UNDETERMINED).
